macro_config.why_depth: Every forward step is one rule application along the single safe branch, so the depth bounds the saturation itself. Measured (scratch/Depth.lean, DepthShipped*.lean, DualDepthOld.lean): at 30, from 16 facts of C, C.dual.dual.dual.CausallyOpenFuture stops at the depth, and the half-lit line's seven facts (one on C.dual^4) with goal C.dual^5.CausallyOpenFuture (refuted) end at the depth; at 60 the first closes and the second fails by exhaustive search. The dual tactician's 12-conjunct goal about C.dual and C.dual.dual (7 facts), which stopped at 30, closes at 60.
macro_config.why_safe_prefix: Read in aesop's source: maxSafePrefixRuleApplications bounds only expandSafePrefix, which handleNonfatalError runs after a failed search to build the error message (Aesop/Search/Main.lean, ExpandSafePrefix.lean). It changes no verdict; raised to 200 as the audit proposed. No measured run changed time with it (k=5 reversals: 3.37 s at depth 30/prefix 50, 3.51 s at 60/50, 3.52 s at 60/200).

fact_rules.design: A checked [[fact]] of sort causality becomes a `safe apply` rule (closes a goal `P t` for ANY causality term t: fvar, C.dual, a constant such as Causal.timelikeLine; its standing instances are synthesised and the rule fails, leaving no goal, where synthesis fails; terminal and fail-fast: no simp, no unfolding). When the fact's property is a premise of an emitted edge, it is also a `safe forward` rule with `(pattern := <its causality binder>)`, so it holds of every causality term in sight and feeds the conjunctive edges (the pattern writes no new term). Conditions (emitted_facts): checked; property of the ladder, sort causality, with a Lean form; standing words in the vocabulary; witness found in an ETT-layer module (model_path None); witness a theorem whose ONE explicit binder is the causality, `(C : Causality M)` or a Precausality, read off the new lean_index key `tsigs` (fact_binder); the binder's name is the pattern's. Generic: nothing is specific to curves_extend.
fact_rules.why_apply_not_forward: Measured on the then-shipped Test.lean (352 examples) with Dual imported (4.73-4.75 s): the fact curves_extend as a forward rule with pattern C: 16.56-17.03 s; forward without pattern (immediate C): 16.20 s; forward with pattern but a sorry'd stand-in taking no instance: 5.86 s; as a safe apply rule: 5.29-5.35 s; the import of its module alone: 4.67-4.70 s. So the cost is the failing synthesis of T1Space M / SecondCountableTopology M on a bare space (8.45 ms / 7.14 ms each, scratch/Synth.lean), repeated at every goal of every search in which a causality is in sight. The apply form pays it only on goals of the fact's own form.
registered_in_Test_only: curves_extend: Causal.Causality.curvesExtend_of_t1_secondCountable (binder C), standing T1, second_countable, apply only (no emitted edge reads curves_extend). Not in Rules: its module Causal.CurvesExtendSecondCountable is ETT-layer (model_path None) but imports Causal.Ladder.Rules: Causal.CurvesExtendSecondCountable → Causal.MaximalZorn → Causal.ErsMughd → Causal.Ladder.Rules. Rules.lean importing it would be an import cycle. Rules.lean carries a `-- skipped fact ... cycle: ...; Causal.Ladder.Test registers it locally` line; Test.lean imports the module and registers `attribute [local aesop safe apply ...]` inside its own section.

aesop_could_not: Ship curves_extend: not aesop's limit but the module graph. Rules.lean cannot import Causal.CurvesExtendSecondCountable, which imports Rules through MaximalZorn → ErsMughd. The fact is tested in Test.lean only; elsewhere C.CurvesExtend is still discharged by the term (kb/0221 stands). Proposal 1 breaks the cycle.

Cheap forward rules with instance arguments: aesop re-attempts a forward rule's instance synthesis at every goal of the search, and a failing synthesis costs ~8 ms on a bare space (not reused across aesop's goals in what I measured): a fact matching every causality made Test.lean 3.5 times slower. Hence apply-only unless an emitted edge reads the fact. A future fact WITH standing that an edge reads will pay this; absolutely_minimal is expected with none.

Deep nested reversals in a large context: from 16 facts of C, C.dual^5.CausallyOpenFuture (provable) still stops at depth 60 after 3.4 s, and C.dual^7 exceeds the 200000-heartbeat budget (timeout in isDefEq, 6.1 s). Neither limit helps (each reversal level receives every two-sided fact, ~16 forward steps per level); assumptionTransparency := .reducible does not help either (the C.dual^7 timeout moves to whnf); the profiler gives typeclass inference 0.98 s of 3.79 s at k=5. Real uses carry one or two reversals.
The forward form of a fact is chosen by the emitted EDGES that read it; Dual.lean's hand-written introductions (premises: the one-sided nodes) are not consulted. No fact concerns a one-sided node.
fact_binder reads sources, not elaborated types: a witness whose causality comes from a `variable` line, or that takes a second explicit argument, is skipped (`shape`), never emitted wrongly.
A standing word stronger than needed (T2 where T1 suffices) is still not detected: the new one-word drops detect a word that is not needed at all.
maxSafePrefixRuleApplications cannot speed up or change a verdict: it only bounds the post-failure expansion for the message.

kb_proposals: causal_ladder's facts (T-tac-ladder-integration): a checked [[fact]] of sort causality is a safe apply rule under its standing (closes P t for any causality term), and also a safe forward rule with the rule pattern of its causality when an emitted edge reads it. curves_extend's rule is not in Causal.Ladder.Rules (its module imports Rules through MaximalZorn → ErsMughd): Causal.Ladder.Test registers it locally; kb/0221 stands until the cycle is broken.

An aesop forward rule with instance arguments that matches everywhere (a fact on every causality) pays a failing instance synthesis (~8 ms for T1Space M on a bare space) at every goal of every search: Test.lean went from 4.7 s to 16.8 s. Make such a rule goal-directed (safe apply) unless another rule must read it.

Update of kb/0225: causal_ladder now runs aesop at maxRuleApplicationDepth 60 (maxSafePrefixRuleApplications 200, which only bounds the post-failure expansion behind the error message).
